Being a leader comes with responsibilities and obligations. There are a lot of essential qualities a leader must possess, but a few stand out more than others. Namely, the most important qualities of a leader are empathy, virtue and insight.

To begin with, empathy is something a leader needs to maintain a reliable bond with their crew. This means viewing from others' perspectives, and taking measures to suit everybody's needs as best as possible. If a leader feels superior and fails to notice other people's contributions or difficulties, they won't be able to know their team well enough to represent each individual. Furthermore, study shows that 89% of employees in a large scale company believe their boss can't handle working in their positions for even one day. Therefore, being empathetic often requires a leader to place others' emotions prior to theirs, and earn everyone's trust through proving that even someone with a leadership title can master the most basic skills. 

Secondly, virtuous intentions and actions of leaders are indispensable as well. While some may believe the prosperity of an organisation sometimes relies on taking morality risks, it is stated that in 2021, almost two thirds of those who participate in any kind of criminal or immoral activity end up unsuccessful, or worse, arrested. Leaders take initiative in decision making, and a lack of virtue behind those decisions can impact the entire population involved, not just the leader themselves. Selfishness in leaders is also extremely destructive, because it is closely related to the fate of each person under the leader's authority. A leader can only make sound judgements considering the group's interest as a whole when they are truly selfless and virtuous.

Moreover, it is equally important for anyone in the leadership role to have insight. Which in this case, is the vision and intelligence of a leader. Leadership ability demands a clear plan for the present and future, and the wit in the plan development process. Adam Chan, the CEO of an electronics brand, claims: "Leaders can't be leaders until they learn to be insightful, and work their way around challenges with that vision in mind." Some people might have more well rounded intellectual instincts and insightful thoughts than others, but what differentiates a leader and those in subordinate places is the wise use of their insight in decision making and plan developing. A leader must not primarily focus on immediate accomplishments or temporary satisfaction. Instead, it is the consideration for beyond the present in a leader that gains trust and respect.

To wrap up, the leadership role is harsh and demanding. Part of the reason why is that the most important qualities of a leader are empathy, virtue and insight. Without these qualities, it is nearly impossible for leaders to guide their team towards the right direction.

There have been many great leaders throughout history. Analysing these historical figures allows one to identify the key traits possessed by a great leader. The most important qualities a leader should possess are; collaboration, taking initiative, and being responsible. 

Being collaborative and working well with your fellow colleagues and peers is necessary to produce good results. An example of a leader who demonstrates collaboration successfully is M.S Dhoni. As a former captain of the Indian cricket team, his role as a leader was crucial in the team's overall success. Being a part of a team required him to collaborate with his fellow teammates to ensure they produce their highest quality cricket. His tasks ranged from working with his team and understanding their strengths and weaknesses, to collaborating with coaches to analyse other teams, creating an effective game plan. Overall his collaboration allowed him to lead his team to many victories in the game of cricket, making many recognise his brilliance as a leader. 

Another important quality of a leader is taking initiative. As a leader, one must be able to take charge and ensure the task at hand gets completed. Without this ability to take the initiative, tasks may be left unfinished, and members on the team, or supporters, are left without the drive to strive and move forward with their tasks or goals. An example of a leader who displays great initiative is Steve Jobs. Although, he was known as a harsh leader, he was able to produce the best results from his employees and created a highly successful company. He was able to achieve this by taking the initiative to develop ideas and delegate tasks to those he thought fit. His hard work and display of initiative motivated his employees to produce their best work as well. Many regard Steve Jobs as a revolutionary, due to his impact in the world of technology. However, this would not be possible without his leadership, shown through his ability to take the initiative. 

Finally, showing responsibility is another major quality a  leader should display. Being a leader many people respect is not easy. However, taking responsibility for failures, and crediting others for success is one way to start. A prime example of this is, Barack Obama. The former president was an exceptional leader, loved by many. Throughout his time in office he accomplished many feats, yet he never credited himself. After winning the election to be the next president, Obama thanked his party members and the people of America who voted for him. However, after the 9/11 incident, he took the blame and responsibility for the attack, working hard to serve justice for those who took part in this tragic event. This show of responsibility touched the hearts of many, earning him the respect and loyalty of many Americans. To this day Obama is cemented in history as an outstanding leader.

In conclusion, showing collaboration, initiative and responsibility, are the key qualities of a leader. Demonstrating these traits can ensure one's success as a leader in any aspect of life.

 For example, when a manufacturer faces an issue and cannot deliver a company's order on the supply date, the CEO of the company or operations manager, must be flexible. They should have given the manufacturing company an earlier due date when assessing possible risks. If they did not do this, they should be able to delay the launch of these products or have some extras to sell in some of their locations. A club leader must be responsible and ensure that their own work as well as their peers is complete. If they fail to do so, club events, applications, and promotions would be delayed. As a result of waiting patiently, and not rejecting an idea instantly, said idea may turn out beautifully.
